sections.label: Foreign-trained dentists proportion rise
sections.summary: The proportion of foreign-trained dentists in Singapore rose from 20% in 2008 to 36% in 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: The proportion of foreign-trained dentists in Singapore has risen steadily from 20%, or about 302 out of 1,484 dentists in 2008, to 36%, or 900 out of 2,475 dentists in 2019.

sections.label: Dental Registration Act amendments
sections.summary: The Bill amends the DRA to require foreign-trained dental graduates to pass a qualifying examination and revises the DRA Schedule.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: First, the Dental Registration Act (DRA) will be amended by this Bill to require that foreign-trained dental graduates must pass a qualifying examination to be eligible for conditional registration; and second, the DRA Schedule will be revised to list the foreign universities whose dental degree holders are automatically eligible to take the qualifying examination.

sections.label: Clause 4 qualifying examination requirement
sections.summary: Clause 4 amends section 14A of the DRA to require foreign-trained dental graduates to pass a qualifying examination for conditional registration.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Clause 4 of the Bill amends section 14A of the DRA to introduce a requirement that foreign-trained dental graduates must take and pass a qualifying examination to be eligible for conditional registration.

sections.label: Amended section 14A requirement
sections.summary: Amended section 14A requires all foreign dental graduates, regardless of DRA Schedule listing, to pass a qualifying examination for conditional registration.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Section 14A, when amended, will make it a requirement for foreign dental graduates, regardless of whether their qualifications are contained in the DRA Schedule, to pass a qualifying examination to be eligible for conditional registration.

sections.label: Revision of DRA Schedule
sections.summary: The DRA Schedule, listing foreign dentistry degrees recognised by the Singapore Dental Council for conditional registration, will be revised.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: I now move on to the second measure which we will be implementing to ensure the continued quality of foreign-trained dental graduates who practise in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: This will be a revision of the DRA Schedule, which contains the list of foreign degrees in dentistry that are recognised by the Singapore Dental Council (SDC) for the purposes of conditional registration.

sections.label: Schedule revision and transitional period
sections.summary: The Schedule's last revision was 2008; a transitional period will let current qualifications and enrolled students still apply for conditional registration.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: The last revision of the Schedule was in 2008 and a review is timely to ensure the continued quality of foreign-trained dental graduates who practise as dentists in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: But I have highlighted this as it complements the introduction of the mandatory qualifying examination that foreign-trained dental graduates must pass to be eligible for conditional registration.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: There will be a transitional period after the revision of the Schedule, where qualifications in the current Schedule will continue to be recognised and, their holders, as well as students who are already enrolled or have secured places in courses leading to such qualifications, may apply for conditional registration under the DRA.

sections.label: Qualifying examination start date
sections.summary: The qualifying examination requirement is planned to be introduced on 1 January 2029.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: At present, the introduction of the requirement for the qualifying examination is planned for 1 January 2029.

sections.label: Dentist ratio goal 2017
sections.summary: In 2017 the Ministry set a goal of one dentist to 2,200 people due to insufficient locally trained dentists.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As early as 2017, the Ministry recognised that there were not enough locally trained dentists to handle all the demands for dental care and set the goal of achieving a ratio of one dentist to 2,200 people.

sections.label: Section 14A foreign dentistry graduates
sections.summary: The amendment expands the requirement to all foreign dentistry graduates, and the SDC website states applicants have two attempts within 12 months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The amendment to section 14A will expand this requirement to all graduates with foreign dentistry degrees, whether specified in the Schedule or not.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The SDC’s website states that an applicant only has two attempts at the qualifying examination which must be taken within 12 months of each other.

sections.label: Progress on dentist ratio goal
sections.summary: The question asks the Minister to share more details on progress toward the one dentist to 2,200 people ratio.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister share more details about its progress in meeting the goal of the ratio of one dentist to 2,200 people?

sections.label: Registering foreign dentistry graduates
sections.summary: The speech focuses on the proposal to register foreign dentistry graduates who pass a qualifying examination before conditional registration.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For my speech, I will focus on the proposal to register all graduates who hold a foreign degree in dentistry, to pass a qualifying examination before they are granted conditional registration to practise as dentists in Singapore.

sections.label: Prospective policy for accepted students
sections.summary: The speaker believes the policies should be carried out prospectively, considering students already accepted or delayed by National Service.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: They did so, particularly aiming for these universities, so they would not need to take the qualifying examinations.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Therefore, I believe it is only fair to carry out these policies prospectively, giving them a few years, taking into account students who have already been accepted into these universities or who are unable to start the degree programme yet due to circumstances, such as National Service.

sections.label: Qualifying exam attempt limit
sections.summary: Guidelines allow the qualifying examination to be taken at most twice, and failing it leaves graduates practically unable to practise dentistry in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The current guidelines dictate that the qualifying examination may be taken a maximum of two times.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The serious implication that we must take into account is that after failing these qualifying examinations, the young graduate is, practically, unable to practise dentistry in Singapore.

sections.label: Foreign-trained dentist proportion rise
sections.summary: Foreign-trained dentists rose from 20% in 2008 to 36% in 2019, with 900 of 2,475 dentists foreign-trained in 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: The proportion of foreign-trained dentists in Singapore had risen significantly from 20% in 2008 to 36% in 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: In 2019, 900 out of a total of 2,475 dentists were foreign-trained.

sections.label: Dentist-to-population ratio target
sections.summary: Dentist numbers depend on the target ratio of one dentist to 2,200 people; the current ratio is one to 2,304, improved from one to 3,215 in 2010.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Ultimately, how many local and overseas trained dentists we need is contingent on the target dentist-to-population ratio.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: I understand MOH’s target ratio is one dentist to 2,200 people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Currently, our dentist to population ratio is one is to 2,304, an improvement from one is to 3,215 in 2010.

sections.label: Local dentistry intake and subsidies
sections.summary: The current 80 per year does not meet demand, so many students study dentistry abroad, and MOH is asked to revamp the industry and provide more dental care subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: The current number of 80 per year does not meet the demand of Singaporeans for dentists, much less the large number of students who apply for dentistry every year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: As a result, many outstanding students have to pay high tuition fees to study dentistry abroad.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: (In English): Mr Deputy Speaker, Sir, we hope that MOH could revamp the dentistry industry in Singapore and provide more subsidies for dental care.

sections.label: Dentists per residents
sections.summary: Singapore had about 4.1 dentists per 10,000 residents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In Singapore, there were about 4.1 dentists per 10,000 residents.

sections.label: NUS dentistry graduates yearly
sections.summary: Each year there are between 50 and 60 dentistry graduates from NUS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Every year, there are between 50 and 60 dentistry graduates from NUS.

sections.label: Qualifying exam for foreign-trained dentists
sections.summary: Amendments make the QE mandatory for all foreign-trained dental graduates with qualifications in the Schedule, and a Member asks why the approved university list is not refined instead.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The amendments to the Dental Registration Bill make the QE mandatory for all foreign-trained dental graduates with qualifications in the Schedule as well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Can the Minister clarify why the Ministry does not just refine the list of approved universities in the Schedule, to remove the universities that do not produce graduates on par with local graduates, instead of imposing a QE?

sections.label: Dental training pipeline and ratio
sections.summary: The dental training pipeline was increased to meet growing dental care needs and a target ratio of one dentist to 2,200 people by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: To ensure adequate supply and continuity of dental care for Singaporeans, we have also increased our dental training pipeline to meet the growing dental care needs of our ageing population and to ensure a target ratio of one dentist to 2,200 people or 0.45 dentist per1,000 population by 2030.

sections.label: NUS dental intake increase
sections.summary: NUS Faculty of Dentistry annual intake rose 36% from 44 in 2008 to 60 in 2018, and with an intake of 80 this year the target ratio is on track.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The annual intake into the NUS Faculty of Dentistry has increased by 36% from 44 in 2008, to 60 in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Based on our service planning parameters, with the increased dental student intake of 80 this year, we expect to be on track to reach a target dentist-to-population ratio of one to 2,200 by 2030.

sections.label: Cap on QE attempts
sections.summary: Foreign-trained dentists with DRA Schedule qualifications get a cap of two attempts per QE part, with the second within 12 months of the first.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: For other foreign-trained dentists who pursue dental qualifications found in the DRA Schedule and who wish to practise in Singapore, there will be a cap of two attempts to pass each part of the QE, with each second attempt having to be within 12 months of the first attempt.

sections.label: Seven-year transition period
sections.summary: A seven-year transition period lets foreign-trained dentists apply for conditional registration under the existing regime, with the QE effective from 1 January 2029.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Mr Yip Hon Weng was concerned about the timeline for the implementation of the qualifying examination requirement as this may affect existing overseas Singaporean dentistry students.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: But I want to reassure Members that there will be a transition period of seven years whereby foreign-trained dentists will still be able to apply for conditional registration under the existing regime under the current DRA, as the implementation of the qualifying examination is intended to only be effective from 1 January 2029.

sections.label: SDC curates recognised qualifications list
sections.summary: SDC will remove 27 schools with no registrations in 12 years, cutting the Schedule from 89 to 62, with the revised Schedule available by end 2021.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Given that the majority of our foreign-trained dentists have graduated from a selected number of foreign dental schools, SDC will curate a more concise list of recognised basic dental qualifications to ensure the relevance of the Schedule.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: We will remove 27 schools that SDC has not received any registration over the past 12 years.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The list of overseas dental schools and universities in the Schedule will be reduced from the current 89 to 62.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: SDC will make available the revised Schedule by end 2021.

sections.label: DRA Schedule periodic review
sections.summary: The DRA Schedule can be reviewed periodically.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: On the review for the DRA Schedule, yes, I think we can review it periodically.

sections.label: Qualifying examination for foreign-trained graduates
sections.summary: A qualifying examination would be put in place to ascertain competency, skills and ability of foreign-trained graduates, with Schedule-list graduates eligible if employed, and Singaporeans/PRs able to take it many times.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: What we want to do then is to put in place a qualifying examination where we can ascertain the actual quality, in terms of competency, skills and ability to perform a procedure, for example, of a foreign-trained graduate.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: In fact, actually, if the graduates are from the Schedule list after this amendment and they can secure employment, they will all, automatically, be eligible for the qualifying examination, the difference being, if you are a Singaporean/PR, you can take it many times.
